project.name: huginn_v1
project.description: Huginn is a financial trade exception processing agent built design-first, using a three-path LangGraph state machine to classify exceptions, retrieve relevant SOPs from a Chroma vector store, and call the Claude API for confidence-scored resolution or escalation decisions.

nodes.name: graph.py
nodes.summary: Constructs and compiles the LangGraph three-path state machine for trade exception triage, wiring conditional routing for invalid-type fast-exit, mandatory escalation fast-exit, and the standard classify-retrieve-reason-decide-log path.

nodes.name: nodes.py
nodes.summary: Implements all LangGraph node functions for the Huginn agent: exception classification, SOP chunk retrieval, Claude-powered LLM reasoning, confidence-based decision making, fast-exit escalation, and structured audit logging.

nodes.name: state.py
nodes.summary: Defines the AgentState TypedDict that carries all shared state across the LangGraph pipeline, including exception payload, classification results, LLM outputs, confidence scores, and audit fields.

nodes.name: test_agent.py
nodes.summary: Comprehensive unit and integration test suite covering the classify, decide, and escalate_fast_exit nodes individually, plus end-to-end graph execution tests verifying audit log and escalation queue outputs.

nodes.name: test_agent_smoke.py
nodes.summary: Smoke test suite that invokes the compiled graph end-to-end against real fixtures to verify the agent produces valid outcomes without mocking the LLM or retrieval layers.

nodes.name: should_fast_exit
nodes.summary: Conditional routing predicate that checks whether the exception type is invalid and should be immediately fast-exited without further processing.

nodes.name: should_escalate
nodes.summary: Conditional routing predicate that checks whether a triggered keyword mandates immediate escalation, bypassing the standard LLM reasoning path.

nodes.name: build_graph
nodes.summary: Assembles and compiles the full LangGraph StateGraph by registering all node functions, setting the entry point, and wiring conditional and unconditional edges for all three execution paths.

nodes.name: classify
nodes.summary: Classifies a trade exception by type and scans its description for mandatory-escalation keywords (sanctions, AML, regulatory hold), setting exception_type, exception_sub_type, and triggered_keyword on the state.

nodes.name: retrieve_node
nodes.summary: Queries the Chroma RAG retriever with the exception description to fetch the most relevant SOP document chunks, storing them and the source document ID on state.

nodes.name: reason
nodes.summary: Invokes Claude via the Anthropic API with a structured prompt containing the exception details and retrieved SOP chunks, then parses the JSON response to extract confidence score and reasoning trace.
nodes.languageNotes: Calls anthropic.Anthropic() directly with os.environ for the API key and parses raw LLM JSON output with manual string cleaning before json.loads.

nodes.name: decide
nodes.summary: Applies a confidence threshold to determine whether the exception should be auto-resolved or escalated, setting the outcome field on state.

nodes.name: escalate_fast_exit
nodes.summary: Handles mandatory escalation fast-exit path by setting the ESCALATED outcome and nulling LLM-specific fields that were never populated, then calling the audit logger.

nodes.name: log_result
nodes.summary: Assembles a structured audit record from all state fields and writes it to the audit log, forming the terminal node for every execution path through the graph.

nodes.name: AgentState
nodes.summary: TypedDict defining the complete shared state contract for the LangGraph pipeline, with 14 typed fields covering the exception payload, classification outputs, retrieval results, LLM reasoning, confidence score, and decision outcome.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses TypedDict rather than a dataclass or Pydantic model, keeping it compatible with LangGraph's state channel protocol.

nodes.name: TestClassifyNode
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the classify node, covering price mismatch, quantity mismatch, and keyword detection for sanctions, AML, and regulatory hold including case-insensitivity.

nodes.name: TestDecideNode
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the decide node verifying auto-resolve at and above threshold and escalation below threshold, on None confidence, and at zero confidence.

nodes.name: TestEscalateFastExitNode
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the escalate_fast_exit node verifying it sets the correct ESCALATED outcome and nulls LLM fields.

nodes.name: TestAgentGraph
nodes.summary: End-to-end integration tests for the compiled graph covering the fast-exit sanctions path, standard price and quantity mismatch paths, and assertions on audit log and escalation queue file outputs.

nodes.name: make_initial_state
nodes.summary: Test helper that constructs a fully initialized AgentState dict from a fixture exception payload and job ID, pre-populating all optional fields to None.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI application defining the three core endpoints (POST /exceptions, GET /exceptions/{job_id}, GET /escalations) that drive trade exception triage — invoking the LangGraph agent, persisting results to an in-memory store, JSONL audit log, SQLite, and an escalation queue.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a synchronous in-process fake-async pattern: the LangGraph agent is invoked synchronously inside the async FastAPI handler, and results are stored in a module-level dict (_result_store) instead of a real async job queue.

nodes.name: submit_exception
nodes.summary: POST /exceptions handler that deserializes the incoming TradeException, invokes the Huginn LangGraph agent synchronously, persists the triage result to the in-memory store, JSONL audit log, and SQLite database, and returns a job ID with outcome.

nodes.name: get_exception_result
nodes.summary: GET /exceptions/{job_id} handler that retrieves a previously processed triage result from the in-memory result store, returning 404 if the job ID is unknown.

nodes.name: get_escalations
nodes.summary: GET /escalations handler that reads the escalation queue JSONL file, parses each record, and returns a list of trade exceptions flagged for human review.

nodes.name: exception.py
nodes.summary: Defines the core domain model for trade exceptions, including the TradeException Pydantic model with field validation and three supporting enums (ExceptionType, SettlementMismatchSubType, Severity) used across the API and agent layers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Pydantic v2 BaseModel with a model_validator for cross-field validation (sub_type must be set only when type is SETTLEMENT_MISMATCH), and str-based Python Enum subclasses for type safety.

nodes.name: TradeException
nodes.summary: Pydantic v2 model representing a trade exception with seven fields (exception_id, trade_id, type, sub_type, description, timestamp, severity) and a cross-field validator ensuring sub_type is only present for settlement mismatch exceptions.

nodes.name: test_api.py
nodes.summary: Comprehensive integration test suite for all three FastAPI endpoints, covering happy-path responses, schema validation, 422/404 error cases, agent routing paths (standard vs fast-exit), and persistence side-effects (audit JSONL, SQLite, escalation queue).

nodes.name: TestAPIEndpoints
nodes.summary: pytest test class with 17 test methods exercising all three API endpoints via a TestClient, including fixture-driven happy-path tests, error cases, agent routing assertions, and side-effect persistence checks.

nodes.name: test_schema_smoke.py
nodes.summary: Standalone smoke test script that instantiates TradeException from five fixture files to verify Pydantic validation accepts valid payloads and correctly rejects an invalid type fixture with a ValidationError.

nodes.name: index.py
nodes.summary: Provides a lazy singleton accessor for the Chroma vector store, initializing HuggingFace embeddings and the persisted Chroma collection on first call and caching the instance for subsequent calls.

nodes.name: get_vectorstore
nodes.summary: Lazily initializes and returns the Chroma vector store singleton backed by all-mpnet-base-v2 embeddings; subsequent calls return the cached instance.

nodes.name: retriever.py
nodes.summary: Exposes the single public RAG retrieval function retrieve(), which queries the Chroma vector store and returns the top-k matching document chunks with metadata and similarity scores.

nodes.name: retrieve
nodes.summary: Queries the vector store with the given text and returns a list of up to top_k dicts containing document_id, sub_type, text, and similarity_score fields.

nodes.name: test_mimir.py
nodes.summary: Unit test suite for the Mimir retriever covering correct document retrieval for each mismatch sub-type, required chunk fields, empty-list safety, and top_k parameter behavior.

nodes.name: TestMimirRetrieve
nodes.summary: Test class with six test methods exercising retrieve() against price, quantity, and settlement-date mismatch queries, as well as field-presence, empty-result safety, and top_k constraints.

nodes.name: test_mimir_smoke.py
nodes.summary: Script-style smoke test that runs three labelled queries through retrieve() and asserts the top result matches the expected document_id, sub_type, text, and similarity_score for each; acts as a gate before Subplan 3.
nodes.languageNotes: Implemented as a top-level script rather than a unittest/pytest class, with sys.path manipulation for direct execution outside a test runner.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: README.md establishes the project's defining idea: design comes first, code is secondary. Huginn is a financial trade exception processing agent — it classifies discrepancies between internal and counterparty records, retrieves relevant SOPs, reasons over them using the Claude API, and either auto-resolves or escalates to a human reviewer. Reading this first anchors every subsequent code step in its business purpose.
tour.languageLesson: This project was built design-first: the architecture document, interface contract, and all 28 design decisions were locked before any code was written. The README is the primary signal of that methodology, not just a setup guide.

tour.title: Architecture & Design Decisions
tour.description: DESIGN.md and DESIGN_DECISIONS.md together form the specification layer that governed every implementation choice. DESIGN.md covers the five components and the three-path state machine topology. DESIGN_DECISIONS.md registers all 28 locked decisions with their reasoning and rejected alternatives — reading it reveals why the code looks the way it does before you see a single line of it.

tour.title: Interface Contract
tour.description: INTERFACE_CONTRACT.md is the pre-implementation specification that defined every component's inputs, outputs, and data types before coding began. It is the bridge between the architecture narrative (Step 2) and the actual code structures you will encounter starting in Step 4. When you see a Pydantic model or a function signature, this document is why it has exactly those fields.

tour.title: API Entry Point
tour.description: api/main.py is the runtime entry point for the entire system: a FastAPI application with three endpoints — POST /exceptions to submit a new trade exception, GET /exceptions/{job_id} to retrieve a triage result, and GET /escalations to list exceptions that require human review. This file is where the domain model (exception.py) and the agent graph (graph.py) are assembled into an HTTP-accessible service, and where every end-to-end execution begins.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI uses Python type annotations as the source of truth for request and response validation. Declaring a Pydantic model as a route parameter means FastAPI automatically validates incoming JSON, generates OpenAPI docs, and returns a 422 with structured errors on bad input — without any manual validation code.

tour.title: Domain Model
tour.description: models/exception.py defines the TradeException Pydantic model and its three supporting enums: ExceptionType, SettlementMismatchSubType, and Severity. These types are the vocabulary shared across every layer — the API deserializes requests into TradeException objects, the agent's state machine carries them, and the audit logger persists them. The model enforces field-level validation at the boundary, so invalid exceptions are rejected before they ever reach the agent.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic v2 models use Python type annotations with validators for runtime enforcement. Enums as field types mean only declared values are accepted — Python will raise a ValidationError at instantiation time if the caller passes an unknown exception type, preventing garbage-in from propagating into the pipeline.

tour.title: Agent State
tour.description: agent/state.py defines AgentState, the TypedDict that every node in the LangGraph pipeline reads from and writes to. It holds the original exception payload, classification results, retrieved SOP chunks, the raw LLM response, confidence score, final decision, and audit fields. Understanding AgentState is the prerequisite for understanding any node — it is the shared contract that makes the state machine's nodes loosely coupled.
tour.languageLesson: LangGraph uses a TypedDict (not a dataclass or Pydantic model) for agent state because TypedDicts support incremental updates: each node returns only the keys it modifies, and LangGraph merges the partial update into the existing state. This enables fan-out parallelism and makes each node independently testable.

tour.title: Three-Path State Machine
tour.description: agent/graph.py wires together the LangGraph state machine that is the core of Huginn's logic. It compiles three distinct execution paths: the invalid-type fast-exit (unknown exception type → immediate rejection), the mandatory escalation fast-exit (sanctions or AML keywords → immediate escalation without LLM reasoning), and the standard path (classify → retrieve SOPs → LLM reasoning → confidence-based decide → log). The graph structure itself encodes the business rules about when AI reasoning is appropriate and when a deterministic rule must fire instead.
tour.languageLesson: LangGraph's conditional_edge() takes a router function that inspects the current state and returns the name of the next node to visit. This is how all three paths diverge from a single classification node — the router examines the exception type and content, and LangGraph dispatches to the correct downstream node without any explicit if/else in the node implementations themselves.

tour.title: Node Implementations
tour.description: agent/nodes.py contains every node function that the graph from Step 7 calls: classify() inspects the exception type and keywords, retrieve_sops() fetches relevant SOP chunks from the Chroma vector store, llm_reason() constructs a prompt and calls the Claude API, decide() thresholds the confidence score to produce a resolution or escalation decision, escalate_fast_exit() handles mandatory escalation, and log_audit() writes the full-fidelity audit record. Each function receives AgentState and returns a partial update — the side-effect-free unit of work in the pipeline.
tour.languageLesson: Each LangGraph node is a plain Python function: it accepts the current state dict and returns a dict of updated keys. This design means nodes are unit-testable in complete isolation — you pass in a hand-crafted state dict and assert on the returned update, with no graph infrastructure required.

tour.title: SOP Knowledge Base
tour.description: The three SOP text files in knowledge_base/raw/ are the domain knowledge that powers the RAG step. SOP-SM-001 covers price mismatch resolution, SOP-SM-002 covers quantity mismatch, and SOP-SM-003 covers wrong settlement date. These plain-text documents are the content that Mimir (Steps 10-11) chunks, embeds, and stores in the Chroma vector store — and what the llm_reason() node (Step 8) receives as context when constructing its prompt to Claude.

tour.title: Mimir RAG Retrieval
tour.description: mimir/retriever.py exposes a single public function retrieve() that takes a query string and returns the top-k matching SOP document chunks from the Chroma vector store. mimir/index.py provides the lazy singleton accessor that initializes HuggingFace embeddings and the Chroma client on the first call, avoiding startup cost until retrieval is actually needed. Together these two files form the Mimir subsystem — the information retrieval layer that gives the LLM relevant procedural context before it reasons about a trade exception.
tour.languageLesson: The lazy singleton pattern (initialize on first call, cache the result) is common in Python services that hold expensive resources like embedding models. A module-level variable initialized to None, replaced on first access, ensures the HuggingFace model is loaded exactly once per process lifetime regardless of how many retrieve() calls are made.

tour.title: Index Build Script
tour.description: scripts/build_index.py is the one-shot offline step that must be run before the agent can retrieve SOPs: it reads the raw SOP text files from knowledge_base/raw/, chunks them, generates HuggingFace embeddings, and persists them into the Chroma vector store. It is not part of the runtime path — it is the setup step that populates the vector store that mimir/index.py will later serve. The separation of index-build from retrieval is a key design decision: the knowledge base is stable between runs, so re-indexing is not done on every request.

tour.title: Audit Logger
tour.description: logger/audit.py is the dual-write audit trail that the log_audit() node (Step 8) calls at the end of every execution path. It writes a structured event to both a JSONL file and a SQLite database, and fans out to a separate escalation queue for any exception that was escalated. The full-fidelity record includes the original exception, the SOP chunks retrieved, the LLM raw response, the confidence score, and the reasoning trace — every artifact needed to reconstruct or audit any triage decision.
tour.languageLesson: Dual-write to JSONL and SQLite serves different access patterns: JSONL is append-only and trivially streamable for log aggregation pipelines, while SQLite supports structured queries (e.g., 'show me all escalated SETTLEMENT_MISMATCH exceptions from today'). Writing to both on every event is a design decision that avoids choosing one access pattern at the cost of the other.

tour.title: Three-Path Test Fixtures
tour.description: The three JSON fixtures in tests/fixtures/ are the concrete test inputs that exercise each execution path in the state machine: fixture_price_mismatch.json drives the standard classify-retrieve-reason-decide-log path, fixture_mandatory_escalation.json triggers the sanctions/AML fast-exit before any LLM call, and fixture_invalid_type.json triggers the immediate rejection for unrecognized exception types. These fixtures are the simplest possible demonstration of the three-path architecture — reading them side-by-side shows exactly which input fields determine which path is taken.

tour.title: Test Suite
tour.description: The test suite covers every layer at multiple levels: test_agent.py provides unit tests for individual nodes (classify, decide, escalate_fast_exit) and end-to-end graph execution tests; test_api.py tests all three FastAPI endpoints via the test client; test_mimir.py and test_mimir_smoke.py validate the retriever against the real vector store; test_logger_smoke.py validates the audit logger; and test_agent_smoke.py and test_schema_smoke.py run full end-to-end passes against the real compiled graph and real fixtures. The separation of unit, integration, and smoke tests reflects the design-first discipline — each layer was specified independently and tested independently.

tour.title: Architecture Reference
tour.description: docs/architecture.md is the comprehensive architecture reference that ties together all the components you have now seen in detail. It documents the same five-component system — API, agent, domain types, Mimir, and audit logger — with component-level diagrams and cross-references to the design decisions from Step 2. After walking through the code, reading this document completes the picture: you can now map every paragraph of the architecture doc directly to the file and function that implements it.
